summary: Mohawk Mountain summit lookout: wooden tower 1922, steel tower 1937; its 7x7 cab now sits on a relay tower. End of fire use conflicts (1988 vs 1970s).

facts.design: 7x7 foot metal cab mounted on a much larger microwave transmission tower (NHLR); wooden summit tower 1922, steel tower 1937

access.note: Summit reached by a marked road and trails in Mohawk State Forest. The cab sits on a communications tower, and no source read says it is open to climbers.

visit.trail_note: Road and trails to the summit are very well marked (NHLR visit report, January 2017).

events.note: Wooden lookout tower built on the summit after a fire destroyed 5,000 acres; a 1922 state report credits the White Memorial Foundation's assistance
A watchman was maintained during the fire season (Bridgeport Telegram item dated July 24, 1924, quoted on the Eastern US lookouts page)
Steel tower erected to replace the 1922 wooden tower (Hartford Courant item dated August 20, 1937); observer kept in all months except winter

Register says aircraft detection phased the tower out in 1988, the last fire tower operated in Connecticut. Cold War CT says seasonal use reportedly ran until the seventies (conflict, see resolved_conflicts)
NHLR visit report dated January 8, 2017: good condition; reports the original tower and a former Booth Hill observation tower removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says aircraft detection phased the tower out in 1988. A Cold War CT page says the tower reportedly ran seasonally until the seventies. Both are reported in the story; no dated source read settles it.

The NHLR description says the original tower, without its cab, stands nearby and is open as an observation site. A January 2017 visit report on the same NHLR page says the original and the Booth Hill tower were removed. The story reports both; the register contradicts itself and the 2017 report is the more recent observation.

notes_for_editor: The end date of fire use (1988 per the register, seventies per Cold War CT) and the fate of the original tower (described as standing in the NHLR text, removed per the 2017 visit report) are unresolved. Living New Deal (search snippet only; the page returned HTTP 403) lists a demolished CCC steel tower at Mohawk State Forest, which is unverified and not used. The Cornwall Historical Society page shows a 1924 photo of Henry Bouteiller at the tower, courtesy of Jean Bouteiller, but no image URL was retrieved, so no photo entry was added. Current condition is only as recent as the January 2017 visit report.
